title: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd - 542830 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; EBITDA margin above 80%, EBIT margin 80.33% vs 84.12%
+33.82% YoY; segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the resignation of Sanjay Jain and assurance on no material discrepancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a completely personal decision, praised his leadership, and said he will continue supporting from outside. No discrepancies were addressed beyond that assurance.

qa_highlights.question: Why third-party bottled water brands are visible on non-AC trains and kiosks, and Rail Neer's incremental revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail Neer is priced at INR14 per bottle; installed capacity is about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after one plant closed (from 18.4 lakh) against supply of about 15.5 lakh. Gaps at mandatory stations are exploited by unauthorised vendors. Augmentation: Ambernath 2 to 3 lakh and Danapur 1 to 2 lakh bottles/day; four new plants at Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi and Bhagalpur, with timelines possibly spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Catering attachment rates, opt-in/opt-out mix and passenger-experience steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Opt-out for prepaid-train catering is roughly 15-30% (later said 25-30%, unconfirmed). Complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals. E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day from 1.05 lakh; e-pantry is live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100. Branded players are at policy-formulation stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Tejas rebranding and tourism margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC runs two private Tejas trains; non-fare revenue from naming and wrap rights is a policy-backed lever, with the Tejas naming done for the first time. It was described as a previously dormant revenue stream now being promoted through regional and zonal offices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the catering revenue increase in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Catering revenue rose from INR547 crore to INR732 crore, a delta of about INR185 crore. Onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore, licence fees from prepaid and other trains to INR224 crore from INR192 crore, static units to INR33 crore from INR20 crore, e-catering to INR22 crore from INR9 crore, and election specials to INR41 crore from INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the payment aggregator licence (IRCTC Payments) and monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The final RBI application was submitted by the 4 August 2026 deadline, together with the SAR and MVP; RBI response is expected within this financial year, and a TSP is engaged. Current iPay volume is about 2.7 lakh transactions, and expansion would follow once the licence is granted.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of convenience and non-convenience fee, and why the internet ticketing EBIT margin fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience fee rose to INR248 crore from about INR236 crore; non-convenience fee fell to INR113 crore from INR123 crore. Marketing and ad income dipped about INR3 crore (INR14.51 crore to INR11.03 crore), and agent business was restricted. About INR10 crore of maintenance was booked, and NGET infra refresh and active-active DR at Secunderabad are being invested in. EBIT margin was 80.33% vs 84.12%, and management said it normally sits at 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the catering margin decline to 9.29% and the one-time HR cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Proof-of-concept on six trains cost more than INR4 crore. Total HR/gratuity one-time charge was about INR20 crore, of which INR10 crore was booked in catering, covering gratuity (INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh) and post-retirement benefits. Management said this will not recur next quarter, and the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by September (two trains) and November (two trains).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Rail Neer margin decline and how big was the profit impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell from about 14-15% to about 10%, mainly due to resin and petroleum cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis; material cost rose from INR55 crore to INR61 crore. Management said overall profit fell by only about INR4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What share of tourism and internet ticketing revenue comes from OTA partners and other channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Tourism OTA-linked income was about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%), or 5-7% from online hotels and ticketing alone. Internet ticketing revenue excluding convenience fee is about 18% of total revenue, and about 26% including it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected run rate for non-convenience fee and the UPI share of tickets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a quarterly run-rate and said the figure will not revert to INR110-115 crore. It aims to return toward INR150 crore via iPay, the e-wallet loyalty programme (growing more than 200%) and changes to agent associations. UPI share of tickets was 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat catering model and steady-state margin given the GST treatment on prepaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC's model is largely licensing. Vande Bharat catering is outsourced via limited tenders to empanelled licensees, while IRCTC runs catering in 81 Vande Bharat trains. On a Vande Bharat basis, the licence fee plus GST earns about INR105 per unit against INR222 paid to licensees, with about INR11 of non-claimable GST. Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on new train additions and their ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains are expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore). Passenger growth of about 8% year-on-year also supports catering charges. Train additions are a ministry decision.

qa_highlights.question: Why has internet ticketing revenue not grown, and is the convenience fee being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said convenience fee grew about 4.89% quarter-on-quarter and has historically risen 5-7% a year. The UPI fee of INR10-20 is cited as a drag, and credit card and credit line options carry a higher fee of INR15-30. Management said it will push for a higher convenience fee but cannot force a policy decision.

risks_watch: Catering margin recovery to the 10-12% range depends on the proof-of-concept trains ending by September and November and on the one-time HR charge not recurring in Q2.

Internet ticketing EBIT margin (80.33% vs 84.12%) and non-convenience fee (INR113 crore vs INR123 crore) depend on the outcome of the website transformation, reintroduction of ad revenue, and agent business changes; the target of INR150 crore has no timeline.
Convenience fee is fixed by policy and UPI's INR10-20 fee structure is diluting revenue as UPI share rises to 51.22%.
Rail Neer faces third-party brand encroachment at non-mandatory stations and resin/petroleum cost pressure from the West Asia crisis; augmentation timelines may spill into FY28.
RBI response on the IRCTC Payments aggregator licence is expected within FY27; iPay monetisation depends on that approval.
Rising prepaid-train mix carries lower GST-adjusted margins, and the 25-30% opt-out rate has not been confirmed by management.
Management was evasive on the reason for Sanjay Jain's resignation, saying only that it was a personal decision.
key_quotes: It is a problem which is duly recognized by the railways, by IRCTC also, that these PDW should not come.
So the catering margin traditionally have been between 10 % to 12%. So we will try to maintain that.
This thing will not be repeated for the next quarter, because it has already been taken care of in this quarter.
Our convenience fee has always grown. In this quarter also it has grown.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth and the one-time nature of the HR and proof-of-concept costs, but cautious and sometimes evasive on forward non-convenience fee run-rates, Rail Neer timelines and the Sanjay Jain resignation. Many answers were qualitative, with figures given as "offhand" or unconfirmed.
